ben: Heads-up — saw a weird tail-latency pattern in a perfetto capture for the client->gateway->runtime path. Not a simple GPU busy issue; looks like repeated kernel handoffs and KV cache churn for long sequences. Posting the timeline snippet below, cropped around the spike.

ben: perfetto snippet (timestamps are relative ms):
```
0.0  client_send
1.2  gateway_recv
1.5  gateway_dispatch
2.0  runtime_recv
2.3  runtime_kernel_select: fp16_conv
2.8  kernel_launch: fp16_conv (70us)
3.0  runtime_kernel_select: int8_conv
3.4  kernel_launch: int8_conv (90us)
3.6  kvcache_miss_lookup
3.9  runtime_kernel_select: fp16_conv
4.4  kernel_launch: fp16_conv (68us)
4.6  kvcache_evict
4.9  runtime_kernel_select: int8_conv
5.3  kernel_launch: int8_conv (95us)
...
16.7 client_ack
```

ben: Pattern: alternating fp16/int8 kernels within a single request and repeated kvcache miss/evict pairs. End-to-end this multiplies the latency ~4-5x for some requests.

arjun: Oof. Could be the kernel-selection hysteresis is too short and the quantization policy is toggling when sequence length extends into different buckets. Did you repro with nvprof/nsys to correlate SM utilization?

ben: I ran nsys (short) and saw a lot of kernel small-launch overhead — occupancy low on the int8 kernel because it's selecting a narrow tile. nvprof shows these kernels are launched ~15–20x per request in the spike.

maria: Two quick suspects: 1) the batch-boundary rounding in the selector (we recently changed from ceil to floor for batch-shape bucketing), 2) KV cache key normalization: if the prefix hashing changes mid-request we get miss -> fetch -> new key.

lisa: Can you paste the selector config used for that run? Also which quant config (per-layer or global) — we had a change where small layers fall back to int8 for latency savings, but it isn't stable when sequence length crosses 512->768.

ben: Selector config snippet (added to runtime-cfg for that job):
```json
{"batch_buckets": [64,256,512,768,1024], "hysteresis_ms": 1, "quant_mode": "dynamic_per_layer", "kv_cache_ttl_ms": 50}
```

ben: Note hysteresis_ms = 1 (we lowered it last week). That feels suspicious.

arjun: Yeah, 1ms hysteresis is probably too low — on small kernels the selector ends up flipping between variants because the decision events occur ~<1ms apart. Increase to 8–16ms or make it request-granular.

sam: Also the kv_cache_ttl_ms=50 is small; if your runtime is sharded and a late thread rehydrates the cache it might evict the earlier entry. Are you on the multi-eviction path?

ben: The runtime is single-tenant but multi-worker. I saw kvcache_evict events that line up with other requests from same worker — TTL small + frequent small kernels = churn.

maria: For repro: try increasing hysteresis to 20ms and kv_cache_ttl_ms to 500, then run a perfetto capture + nsys. If the tail disappears, we deduce selector thrash + kv TTL.

ben: Will run now. Quick debug note: you can capture perfetto on the gateway + runtime and stitch traces with the request_id. In case anyone needs the commands:
```bash
# runtime capture (short)
perfetto --config runtime_perf_cfg.pbtxt -o /tmp/runtime.trace --timeout 15s
# gateway capture
perfetto --config gateway_perf_cfg.pbtxt -o /tmp/gw.trace --timeout 15s
# stitch script (we have a helper in tools/trace-stitcher)
python tools/trace-stitcher /tmp/gw.trace /tmp/runtime.trace --match-by request_id > /tmp/stitched.trace
```

perf-bot: [alert] perf spike detected for job id 0x7a3f (latency p99 3.2s vs baseline 420ms). Linked trace: https://perfetto.local/trace/0x7a3f :warning:

lisa: If you can repro, also capture the kernel names and parameters from nvprof: `nsys profile -o out -t cuda,osrt --sample=none --trace-fork-exec true` then `nsys stats out.qdrep` — that will give launch stacks.

ben: Quick follow-up after changing hysteresis to 24ms and kv ttl to 300ms — short run (5 requests) reduced p99 from 3.2s -> 520ms. Still a ~25% overhead vs baseline but not 8x. Capturing a longer perfetto + nsys next.

arjun: Sounds like a win. We should consider: default hysteresis to request lifetime for production, or make it adaptive: longer hysteresis when kernel-switch count per request > 1. Also track a metric: kernel_switches_per_request.

maria: Agree. Also add a KV miss heatmap in console (per-request) so we can quickly spot churn hotspots.

ben: I'll file a tiny follow-up PR: bump default hysteresis to 20ms and add a runtime flag `--selector-mode=stable` to prefer fewer switches. Will attach traces to the PR.

sam: If you want, I can instrument a synthetic load generator that ramps sequence length across the thresholds to stress it.

ben: Please do — that will help validate. I'll upload nsys + perfetto artifacts to the bug.

lisa: Nice root cause triangle: low hysteresis + aggressive quant fallback + tiny KV TTL. Thanks for the clear trace. :thumbsup:

ben: Thx — will update once I have the extended traces attached.

sam: ping when uploaded, I'll run the synth across all GPUs tomorrow morning.

ben: Uploaded (links in the bug). End.
